previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with secondary progressive multiple sclerosis and neurogenic bladder managed with a chronic Foley catheter, was admitted for weakness and fatigue, which he recognized as typical symptoms of a urinary tract infection. He reported transient hematuria and had not been taking his methenamine due to a lapse in prescription. Initial labs showed marked leukocytosis and pyuria, prompting IV antibiotics and fluid resuscitation. A chest X-ray ruled out pneumonia. His Foley catheter was replaced, and he was started on broad-spectrum antibiotics. Urine culture grew Escherichia coli, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Enterococcus species. Antibiotics were de-escalated to oral ciprofloxacin and amoxicillin-clavulanate based on sensitivities, with addition of methenamine for prophylaxis. His symptoms resolved, and he returned to baseline. He was discharged home with home services, continuing all baseline medications and a plan for follow-up with his primary care provider.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo M with MS on monthly solumedrol, neurogenic bladder, 
chronic indwelling foley and recurrent UTIs with ESBLs and VSE 
who is admitted with fatigue and generalized weakness and found 
to have UTI.

# UTI: He has recurrent UTIs with a neurogenic bladder and a 
chronic indwelling foley. He was symptomatic and treated with 
vancomycin and cefepime. Urine cultures returned a E. Coli 
species susceptible to bactrim. He was discharged with a 11 day 
course of bactrim DS (for a total of 14 days of antibiotics). 
His fatigue and weakness completely resolved. He was also 
discharged on methenamine and with ___ to assist with foley 
changes in attempt to decrease the amount of UTIs.

# Fatigue/weakness: likely due to UTI. Resolved with hydration 
and treatment.

#Diarrhea: Resolved in the hospital. Stool studies were negative 
for infection.

#Multiple sclerosis: Secondary progressive type. Continue prior 
treatment.

#Depression: continued fluoxetine.
